clue.text: Yak lying down on bedding

indicators.note: in an across clue, something resting on another thing comes after it, so the second piece follows the first

parts.note: a pillow is part of the bedding
to yak is to chatter

explanation.surface: A shaggy Himalayan ox has flopped down on someone's sheets.
explanation.walkthrough: Yak looks like the animal, but it is the verb for chattering; the whole clue also describes the answer, chat while lying in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Pillow talk is the intimate, relaxed conversation lovers share in bed, which is idle chatter while lying on bedding.

clue.text: Seabird dropping in gust

indicators.note: to drop something is to let it go, so these letters leave the word

parts.note: a puffin is a seabird
taken as written, the letters removed

explanation.surface: A seabird is caught by a gust and falls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropping in' reads as a bird swooping down, but 'in' is the very pair of letters taken off the end of the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A puff is a short sudden burst of wind or breath, the same thing as a small gust.

clue.text: Thrash metal ultimately driving out Erica's first husband

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the word is used

parts.note: the last letter of metal

indicators.note: to drive something out is to expel it, so a letter is removed from the word
first points to the opening occurrence, so the letter removed is the one at the very start

parts.note: Erica is the botanical genus of heather
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A heavy metal fan named Erica leaves her first husband for a thrash band.
explanation.walkthrough: Thrash metal is a music genre, but 'Thrash' alone is the definition. Erica is not a woman's name here but the Latin genus of heather; the L takes the place of its opening H.
explanation.definitionFit: To leather someone is an informal British verb for beating them hard, so it means the same as thrash.

clue.text: Words that launch an invention for children?

definitions.text: Words that launch an invention for children?

parts.words: Words that launch an invention for children?
parts.note: surface reading: a slogan for unveiling a new toy or gadget aimed at kids
setter's reading: an invention is a made-up story, and a fairy tale traditionally opens with a set phrase

explanation.walkthrough: 'Invention' suggests a gadget being launched on the market; it means a fiction, and 'launch' means begin the telling.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the conventional opening line of fairy tales and bedtime stories told to young listeners.

clue.text: Worthless type now drunk around noon

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece wraps the other
a drunk person staggers about, so these letters are jumbled out of order

parts.note: the letters as written
N is the abbreviation for noon

explanation.surface: A useless sort of person who is drunk before midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worthless type' reads as a description of a person, but 'type now' is the raw material and only 'Worthless' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Something twopenny costs only two old pennies, so the adjective means cheap, trifling and of little value.

clue.text: Amp taken out of shed slowly

indicators.note: taking something out removes it, so a letter leaves the word

parts.note: a lean-to is a shed built against a wall
A is the abbreviation for ampere

explanation.surface: A guitar amplifier is being carried out of the garden shed at a leisurely pace.
explanation.walkthrough: Amp suggests a guitar amplifier, but it is the unit of current, abbreviated A.
explanation.definitionFit: Lento is the musical tempo direction meaning to be played at a slow pace, from Italian.

clue.text: Some land fenced by Hever Castle to the west

indicators.note: in an across clue west is leftward, so the letters run from right to left
what is fenced in is enclosed, so the answer sits inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Part of an estate enclosed within the grounds of a Kentish castle, on its western side.
explanation.walkthrough: Hever Castle in Kent was Anne Boleyn's childhood home; the fence image makes the enclosure literal.
explanation.definitionFit: An acre is a measured area of ground, 4,840 square yards, so it is a portion of land.

clue.text: Smart Pep keeping Kovacic in the centre for City

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so the outer words hold a letter between them

parts.note: chic means smart or stylish

indicators.note: only the letter sitting at the exact middle of the footballer's surname is kept

parts.note: the fourth of the seven letters in the surname
pep and go both mean energy or vigour

explanation.surface: Pep Guardiola cleverly holding on to midfielder Mateo Kovacic at the heart of Manchester City's team.
explanation.walkthrough: Pep and City steer you to football: Guardiola manages Manchester City, where Kovacic plays. Here Pep is just energy, and City is a different city entirely.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicago is a large American metropolis on Lake Michigan in Illinois, so it is an example of a city.

clue.text: Perhaps lead on a Republican Yankee in primary

parts.note: lead is one example of a chemical element
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for Republican
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A Republican Yankee candidate might take the lead in a primary election.
explanation.walkthrough: The American picture makes primary an election and lead a front position; lead is the metal, and primary means basic.
explanation.definitionFit: Elementary and primary both describe the first, most basic stage, as in elementary or primary schooling.

clue.text: Picked up open old tin

indicators.note: to pick up a sound is to hear it, so the word is taken by how it is heard

parts.note: frank means candid or open

explanation.surface: Someone retrieved an opened old tin can.
explanation.walkthrough: Tin is British slang for money; 'old' because the French franc was replaced by the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: The franc was the currency of France before the euro, so it is money no longer in use.

clue.text: Graves will probably be dug by this aficionado

definitions.text: Graves will probably be dug by this aficionado

parts.note: surface reading: someone with a fondness for excavating burial plots
setter's reading: Graves is a Bordeaux wine region, and to dig something is slang for liking it

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a gravedigger or a ghoulish enthusiast; Graves is a wine, and dug means enjoyed, as in 'I dig it'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word comes from Greek for wine and loving: a connoisseur who appreciates fine vintages such as Bordeaux reds.

clue.text: Goes off crew in a boat

indicators.note: in means inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a, as in 'five pounds a day', means per
eggs that go off are said to addle
a crew is a team

explanation.surface: The crew of a boat sets off on a voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes off' reads as departing, but it means turning rotten. The little word 'a' is the outer piece: it means per.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddle steamer is a steam-driven vessel propelled by large paddle wheels, a type of boat.

clue.text: Famous person from Hugh Laurie drama and Homeland, possibly

parts.note: Hugh Laurie starred as Dr Gregory House in the US series House

indicators.note: possibly signals one possible rearrangement, so the letters may be reordered

parts.note: the letters of the TV series title

explanation.surface: A star who came from a couple of hit American TV dramas.
explanation.walkthrough: Both shows are real titles; only the second has its letters rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A household name is someone so well known that every family recognises them, a celebrity.

clue.text: This could be present one is expecting

definitions.text: This could be present one is expecting

parts.words: This could be present one is expecting
parts.note: surface reading: a gift someone is waiting to receive
setter's reading: present is a grammatical tense, and 'expecting' is itself an example of a verb form ending in -ing

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about an anticipated gift; read as grammar, 'present' is a tense and the word 'expecting' is an instance of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A participle is a verb form used as an adjective or in compound tenses; the present kind ends in -ing.

clue.text: Crack radius and maybe ulna when Gloucester's back goes in flying

indicators.note: going in means entering, so one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: crack means first-rate, A1, written AI in crosswords
R is the abbreviation for radius
the ulna is one example of a bone

indicators.note: the back of a word is its end, so only the final letter is used

parts.note: the final letter of the city name

explanation.surface: A player fractures arm bones when Gloucester's full-back dives in, in a rugby match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' looks like a fracture next to the arm bones, but it means first-class: A1, with the 1 read as I. Gloucester is a famous English rugby club.
explanation.definitionFit: Something airborne is carried through the air, so it is in flight, the same as flying.

clue.text: Close to second adult quitting mission, extremely strict

indicators.note: to quit is to leave, so a letter departs from the word

parts.note: the Alamo in Texas was a Spanish mission
A is the abbreviation for adult; the second of its two occurrences is the one to go

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only the outer letters are used

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Near to the moment a senior officer abandons a very rigorous mission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like a moment of time, but it picks out which of the two As in the mission is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Almost means nearly, very nearly reaching a point, so it is synonymous with close to.

clue.text: ELO music in play for London theatre

indicators.note: something in play is loose and moving about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: Songs by the Electric Light Orchestra feature in a West End show.
explanation.walkthrough: ELO is the 1970s band, but here it is just three letters for the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: The London Coliseum is a large West End venue, home of English National Opera, on St Martin's Lane.

clue.text: Love piano in which Astaire film?

indicators.note: in means inside, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: which and that are both relative pronouns
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: In which Fred Astaire film does a love song at the piano appear?
explanation.walkthrough: Love and piano look like the song-and-dance content of a musical; they supply O and P.
explanation.definitionFit: Top Hat is the 1935 RKO musical starring Fred Astaire and Ginger Rogers, featuring 'Cheek to Cheek'.

clue.text: Copies last couple of ingredients to go with salmon and bagel

parts.note: a parr is a young salmon
a bagel is ring-shaped, like the letter O

indicators.note: the last couple are the final two, so only the closing pair of letters is used

parts.note: the final pair of letters

explanation.surface: Someone duplicates the final items of a recipe for a smoked salmon bagel.
explanation.walkthrough: A parr is a young salmon in its first freshwater stage; the bagel gives a letter by its shape.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot someone is to repeat their words mechanically, without understanding, so it means imitates.

clue.text: Fragile ego principally smitten with Mars trips

indicators.note: something that trips stumbles and falls about, so the letters tumble into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: principally means chiefly or at the head, so the first letter is used

parts.note: the opening letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: An insecure person is besotted with the idea of travelling to Mars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Principally' sits after 'ego' but works on the next word; 'trips' looks like journeys and is the mixing signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Gossamer is used as an adjective for things extremely light, thin and delicate, like a spider's silk.

clue.text: Tears from crook nabbed by M&S

indicators.note: to be nabbed is to be grabbed and held, so one piece is held inside

parts.note: the letters of the store's name, Marks and Spencer
a crook is a bend or angle

explanation.surface: Someone is in tears after a thief is caught at Marks and Spencer.
explanation.walkthrough: Tears reads as crying, but it is the verb that rhymes with bears. Crook means a bend, as in the crook of an arm.
explanation.definitionFit: To mangle something is to tear or crush it badly out of shape, so mangles means rips apart.

clue.text: King's work involved gripe about messenger

parts.note: Carrie is a Stephen King novel

indicators.note: involved means tangled or complicated, so the letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: the letters as written
on means about, as in a book on birds

explanation.surface: A monarch's job involves complaining about the royal courier.
explanation.walkthrough: King suggests a monarch, but it is the horror novelist Stephen King and his first novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A carrier pigeon is a homing bird trained to fly back with written notes, used to deliver messages.

clue.text: Wake seen in river that runs through York

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for river
the Ouse is the river flowing through York

explanation.surface: A boat's wake is visible on the river flowing through York.
explanation.walkthrough: Wake looks like a boat's trail on the water, but it is the verb; the river is named only by its city.
explanation.definitionFit: To rouse someone is to stir them from sleep, so rouse is a synonym of the verb wake.

clue.text: Price departs, but this keeps The Animals going!

parts.note: a fee is a price charged
d is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: Alan Price leaves the 1960s band The Animals, but something keeps them going.
explanation.walkthrough: Alan Price was the keyboard player who left The Animals in 1965; read lower-case, the animals are livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: Feed is fodder given to livestock, the food that sustains farm creatures and keeps them alive.

clue.text: Practise writing English with hack

parts.note: prose is ordinary writing
to hack is to cut
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Advice for a jobbing journalist: practise writing English.
explanation.walkthrough: Hack looks like a journalist, but it is the verb for chopping. Prosecute here is the older sense, not the legal one.
explanation.definitionFit: To prosecute a trade or activity is to carry it on or pursue it, an older sense of practise.

clue.text: Learner driver stuck in pit, getting AA

indicators.note: something stuck in is lodged inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
a learner driver displays an L plate

explanation.surface: A learner whose car is stuck in a ditch calls the AA for roadside rescue.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA is Britain's Automobile Association, the breakdown service; here it is the initials of the author A. A. Milne.
explanation.definitionFit: A. A. Milne was the English writer of Winnie-the-Pooh, so the initials stand for him by name.

clue.text: Carefree sound of pair in the middle of rendezvous in New York?

indicators.note: a pair from the middle is the two central letters, so only those are used

parts.note: the central pair of its ten letters

indicators.note: the sound of something is how it is spoken, so the letters are said aloud

parts.note: Americans call the last letter zee, not zed

explanation.surface: The relaxed sound of a couple meeting for a date in Manhattan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pair' suggests a couple on a date, but it is two letters; British speakers say zed, so New York is needed for the sound to work.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy means relaxed and free from worry, as in easy-going, so it matches carefree.

clue.text: Captivated, lust misled me occasionally, on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection is a mirror image, so the letters run back to front

parts.note: lust is strong desire

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is used

parts.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: Someone confesses that, now and then, being spellbound by lust has led them astray, looking back.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a rueful confession; the setter's reading reverses the whole string at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To be mesmerised is to be held spellbound, as if hypnotised, so it means captivated or enthralled.
